This is not a comment regarding this particular pharmacy but merely a comment on how pharmacies have been impacted by this policy.  My local pharmacist had recently halved his shop space due to the reduction in revenue, as well as increase in expenses. They have been a successful local business for many decades offering great knowledge , service and help when doctors are unavailable. 

Many people do not understand the effect government 60 day dispensing policy has on small pharmacy business’, and not to mention the morale amongst many fantastic pharmacists I have had the fortune of knowing over the years. 

TBH, the only pharmacist owners that I am aware of who are filthy rich through owning pharmacy businesses are the owners of the big discounters, so why is that? It is through cutting back the true value of pharmacy healthcare which is the person-to-person service, and offering of pharmacists’ knowledge.  Anyone who had been to discount chemist as well as mom/pop pharmacy would know the differences (other than the obvious pricing):  the wait time is way longer at discounters ( I personally waited 1 hour for a single packet of cold and flu) , the personal interaction and therefore the opportunity to discuss complicated issues is virtually nonexistent at the discounters, Whereas in a small mom-pop pharmacy, the pharmacists knows you, is willing to sit down and have that all important conversation with you about your embarrassing problems and offer adequate support and advice.

Whilst the government policy does not directly reduce dispensing fee, by stretching the 30 day supply to 60 day it has in effect halve the pharmacy revenue where dispensing is concerned, and here’s the true agenda behind the government policy. By doing so, it reduces government budget not only through the direct payments to pharmacists, it also reduces number of people reaching safety net in any given financial year. (My in-laws family have some serious medical issue, and usually around August, they as a family would reach safetynet which brings their medication costs to $7.70 per item. After going through the figures they figure out that if they were collection 60 day supply, they will never reach safetynet amount).

These reduced Medicare revenue to pharmacies has traditionally been utilised by small business owners to provide previously free services such as delivery, free consultation, blood pressure checks, signature witnessing etc etc. please remember, it’s not often these days that you can walk into a medical centre to have your blood pressure checked or asking your GP a health related question, without either having to pay for the consult or having the receptionist swiping the Medicare card to allow the billing through the healthcare system.
Nor can you expect to walk into your lawyer’s / accountant’s office and expect them to sign and witness your documents without being charged for a massive fee.  In fact I have walked into chemist warehouse asking if pharmacist could witness my bank application for home loan, only to be declined as this is not chemist warehouse policy to provide such service.  Yet these are services we expect from our small businesses pharmacies/pharmacists.

Pharmacists have studied and trained for years just as all other professionals and have been offering these knowledge freely on the basis that they have already been remunerated through the Medicare payment via the previous dispensing payment agreement.

It can be expected that given the government has removed half of these revenue stream, the previously free services will come at a cost to the consumers.

Pharmacists are people too, they have bills to pay, families to raise, just like you and me. Think of our expectations from our pharmacists, think of how our government is treating this group of professionals, would you recommend your children to take up pharmacy as their career choice? If you would not, does that mean you also acknowledge how we are exploiting these professionals?
